name: Question 4
problem:
A call center manager knows that $40%$ of the calls are complaints. If the manager randomly samples $80$ calls, find a normal approximation for the probability that more than $32$ but fewer than $36$ of them are complaints. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size.

*Note: $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*
worked_solution:
Given a population in which a proportion $p$ of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\overset{^}{\,p}$ can be approximated as

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where the sample size $n$ is much smaller than the population size, $np>5,$ and $n(1-p)>5.$

In our case

- the sample size is $n=80,$ and

- the population proportion is $p=0.4.$

Now, since

$$
np=80(0.4)=32>5
$$

and

$$
n(1-p)=80(1-0.4)=48>5,
$$

and $n=80$ is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & ∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}) \\  & ∼N(0.4,\frac{0.4(1-0.4)}{80}) \\  & ∼N(0.4,0.0030).\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we determine the probability we wish to find. If more than $32$ but fewer than $36$ calls are complaints, then 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{32}{80}<\overset{^}{\,p} & <\frac{36}{80} \\ 0.4\le \overset{^}{\,p} & \le 0.45.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the probability we wish to find is
$P(0.4<\overset{^}{\,p}<0.45).$
So, we convert $\overset{^}{\,p}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.4\le \overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.45) & =P(\frac{0.4-0.4}{\sqrt{0.0030}}<Z<\frac{0.45-0.4}{\sqrt{0.0030}}) \\  & ≈P(0<Z<0.91) \\  & =P(Z<0.91)-P(Z<0.00) \\  & =Φ(0.91)-Φ(0.00)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.4<\overset{^}{\,p}<0.45) & =Φ(0.91)-Φ(0).\end{aligned}
$$

html:
Question 4
?

A call center manager knows that 40% of the calls are complaints. If the manager randomly samples 80 calls, find a normal approximation for the probability that more than 32 but fewer than 36 of them are complaints. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size.

Note: Φ(z) is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.

a
Φ(1.07)−Φ(0.35)
b
Φ(0.91)−Φ(0)
c
Φ(1.91)−Φ(1.65)
d
Φ(1.35)−Φ(0.12)
e
Φ(−1.91)−Φ(0.15)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Given a population in which a proportion p of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion p^ can be approximated as

p^∼N(p,p(1−p)n),

where the sample size n is much smaller than the population size, np>5, and n(1−p)>5.

In our case

  • the sample size is n=80, and

  • the population proportion is p=0.4.

Now, since np=80(0.4)=32>5 and n(1−p)=80(1−0.4)=48>5, and n=80 is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

p^∼N(p,p(1−p)n)∼N(0.4,0.4(1−0.4)80)∼N(0.4,0.0030).

Next, we determine the probability we wish to find. If more than 32 but fewer than 36 calls are complaints, then

3280<p^<36800.4≤p^≤0.45.

Hence, the probability we wish to find is P(0.4<p^<0.45). So, we convert p^ to a standard normal random variable by z-scoring:

P(0.4≤p^≤0.45)=P(0.4−0.40.0030<Z<0.45−0.40.0030)≈P(0<Z<0.91)=P(Z<0.91)−P(Z<0.00)=Φ(0.91)−Φ(0.00)

Therefore,

P(0.4<p^<0.45)=Φ(0.91)−Φ(0).
